summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, multiple sclerosis, ulcerative colitis, and asthma was admitted for her third cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She had a port placed on hospital day two to facilitate treatment, followed by successful methotrexate infusion with bicarbonate hydration and leucovorin rescue. She continued to experience moderate right foot pain, managed with increased gabapentin and oxycodone, likely related to prior chemotherapy or underlying MS. Transaminitis persisted but improved during the admission. A new herpes simplex lesion on the lower lip prompted initiation of acyclovir prophylaxis. A lumbar puncture was performed before discharge to rule out leptomeningeal disease; results were pending. She remained stable, with no acute complications, and was discharged home with follow-up planned.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Herpes simplex without mention of complication
